Triggers.value: A specific texture associated with the event
A specific temperature on the skin

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Being emotionally close or intimate with others
I distract myself with something else

Threat.value: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
Being superalert or watchful or on guard
Even when others tell me I am safe I find it impossible to believe it

Negative Appraisals.value: I have permanently changed for the worse
My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe
I have lost my connection to my community and culture

vignette: John is a 27-year-old African man who has experienced significant trauma in his childhood through physical abuse by a caregiver. This event continues to haunt him, shaping his current fears and behaviors. John now works as an Uber driver, navigating the streets of New York with a heavy heart. The traumatic event John endured was particularly intense due to the specific tactile sensations he remembers vividly—the texture of his abuser's hands, the temperature of their skin on his own body, and the sound of footsteps approaching him. These sensory memories are now potent triggers that can set off a cascade of reactions in his daily life. One evening while driving through Brooklyn, John heard a set of footsteps behind him. Instantly, he felt an overwhelming surge of anxiety. The auditory trigger of footsteps sent him into a state of hyperarousal, and he found himself gripping the steering wheel tightly as if it were the only thing grounding him in reality. This reaction to triggers has led him to employ various maladaptive strategies. For example, when he feels these intense emotions rise, John often isolates himself from others to avoid any form of emotional intimacy. He had come to believe that being close to people only leads to pain and betrayal. In addition to avoiding intimacy, John distracts himself by engaging in risky behaviors—speeding through the streets or taking dangerous routes when driving. These actions help divert his attention away from the overwhelming feelings but inevitably heighten his sense of hypervigilance. He is always on guard, constantly scanning for any signs that might trigger a flashback. The tactile memories also play a significant role in John’s daily life. The sensation of certain textures or temperatures can send him into a state where he feels as though he is back in the moment of abuse. For instance, the cold weather would sometimes make his skin feel like it was being touched by his abuser again, causing him to freeze up and lose focus while driving. John’s belief that he has been permanently damaged for the worse only exacerbates his negative appraisals. He feels as though his body is betraying him; every physical reaction reminds him of the abuse, even when he knows intellectually that he is safe. This feeling of being disconnected from his community and culture further isolates him. What frightens John most is that these negative beliefs have led him to use drugs as a coping mechanism. The substances offer temporary relief but ultimately deepen his sense of disconnection and mistrust. The interplay between his triggers, negative appraisals, threat perceptions, and maladaptive strategies creates a self-reinforcing cycle. Whenever he experiences a trigger, such as the sound of footsteps or the touch of cold air on his skin, it intensifies his hypervigilance and sense of risk. This, in turn, leads him to use drugs to numb himself and avoid intimacy further, which then reinforces his belief that he has been permanently damaged. This cycle has taken a toll on John’s life. He often misses work because the triggers make it too difficult for him to focus while driving, leading to financial stress. His relationships with others have also suffered; he pushes people away out of fear and distrust. The combination of these factors has left him feeling isolated and trapped in a pattern that seems impossible to break. John finally sought help after a particularly intense episode where the memory of footsteps led him into an accident. He is most afraid of never being able to escape his trauma, but he also hopes for a chance at healing and reconnecting with others without the constant fear and hypervigilance dictating his life.
